institution: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
name: Marshallese stick navigation chart
attribution: Marshallese maker unrecorded by name. The Smithsonian records R. Naomi Cannon as donor
date: Collected 1940–1959. Entered the collection on 24 August 2006.
dateKind: Collection window and museum accession date. The making date remains open.
medium: Reeds, bast fibre twine, string and 28 cowrie shells
first: The public record describes a preparation aid that models how ocean swells meet land. The museum says it was used for learning before a voyage.
boundary: The collection window is 1940–1959. Donor R. Naomi Cannon described tying string around breaks. That observation belongs to the object’s condition record. Present navigation depends on local expertise and current conditions.
stake: Shoal Shelf needs a place to put a reading aid on shore. The watch log needs another place for what people actually see at sea.
lower: Halen leaves the reference on the shore learning rail and moves the observed-current chalk beside the lookout. Each has its own task.
upper: Clio separates the collection window, Cannon’s report of a repair and the museum’s account of the preparation aid. The local crew keeps current observations in another binder.
altText: A blank, proportioned outline with measurements of 128 and 100 centimetres. The inventory panel shows 28 shells and the 1940–1959 collection window.

catalogTitle: Näku Dhäruk, Yirrkala bark petition presented 14 August 1963
name: Näku Dhäruk, Dhuwa petition
attribution: Yirrkala artists, Dhuwa moiety, according to the Parliamentary Education Office
date: Dated and presented to the Australian House of Representatives on 14 August 1963.
dateKind: Date of the petition and its presentation by Jock Nelson. It is one of two bark petitions tabled that August.
medium: Bark painting and paper, with typed Yolŋu Matha and English and handwritten signatures
dimensions: Item i in the National Archives record for the paired parliamentary documents
first: On 14 August 1963 Jock Nelson presented this Yolŋu petition for an inquiry into land taken from the reserve for mining without consultation. The Parliamentary Education Office credits the Dhuwa artists.
boundary: The Parliamentary Education Office states that the designs express Yolŋu law. The House received the petition. Yolŋu ownership remained unrecognised under Australian law in the proceedings that followed.
stake: The fictional Shelter has a public index for documentary references. The date someone received a request belongs apart from the decision they made about it.
lower: Halen keeps the date of presentation on the public index and sends readers to the Yolŋu centre for the community account. The rail offers a public reference.
upper: Clio keeps the Dhuwa artists and Jock Nelson’s act of presentation in separate fields. The binder names the Yolŋu account and keeps the receipt apart from the outcome.
altText: Diagram of a blank backing and a paper insert. The label reads Dhuwa, 14 August 1963. A separate receipt card names J. Nelson.

catalogTitle: Näku Dhäruk, Yirrkala bark petition presented 28 August 1963
name: Näku Dhäruk, Yirritja petition
attribution: Yirrkala artists, Yirritja moiety, according to the Parliamentary Education Office
date: Dated and presented to the Australian House of Representatives on 28 August 1963.
dateKind: Date of the separate petition and its presentation by Arthur Calwell. The display paper is a copy made to help preserve the signed original.
medium: Bark painting and paper, with typed Yolŋu Matha and English and handwritten signatures
dimensions: Item ii in the National Archives record for the paired parliamentary documents
first: Arthur Calwell presented the second petition on 28 August 1963. The Parliamentary Education Office separately credits its Yirritja artists.
boundary: The National Archives says copies replaced the typed papers on both bark borders to protect the signatures from fading. Its online view reunites photographs of the originals. The designs remain under Yolŋu cultural authority.
stake: The fictional Shelter is updating its public reference. The two notices share an issue and have separate dates and attributions. The reader needs to see where the archive describes the copies.
lower: Halen puts the 28 August public reference on its own line and gives a link to the Yolŋu centre. Visitors can keep it separate from the 14 August entry.
upper: Clio files a Yirritja leaf with Arthur Calwell’s presentation and the copy-history note. The linked references keep the displayed paper and the original signed paper in distinct fields.
altText: Diagram of a blank backing and a paper insert. The label reads Yirritja, 28 August 1963. Stacked papers distinguish the display copy and signed paper.
